The text highlights the tension between societal expectations and personal desires in 'Pride and Prejudice', illustrating how diverse reader backgrounds shape interpretation. Feminist readers may view Elizabeth Bennet as a symbol of women's agency, celebrating her independence, while traditionalist readers might prioritize the novel's emphasis on social standing and family reputation. This contrast demonstrates that literary themes are not static but are filtered through the lens of the reader's own values and cultural context.
